# Hospitals

This folder catalogs the individual Danish hospitals and hospital networks that report clinical data to the Acute Surgery Database (AKDB). The pages contain detailed performance metrics, process indicator compliance, and risk-adjusted mortality outcomes—such as 30-day and 90-day mortality stratified by Charlson comorbidity scores—for each institution. Several hospitals are specifically highlighted in the source reports as "best practice" reference units for exceptional longitudinal improvements in postoperative survival, early mobilization, and epidural pain management, while others are noted for data quality limitations due to low surgical volumes or their specialized tertiary functions.

## Pages

- [[aalborg-universitetshospital-thisted|"Aalborg Universitetshospital, Thisted"]] — Department-level acute surgery data and indicator results for the Thisted unit.
- [[aalborg-universitetshospital|Aalborg Universitetshospital]] — Comprehensive performance metrics on acute surgery indicators, including 30-day mortality and Charlson score stratifications.
- [[aarhus-universitetshospital|Aarhus Universitetshospital]] — Acute surgery outcomes highlighting high epidural anesthesia rates and detailed mortality metrics.
- [[amager-og-hvidovre-hospital|Amager og Hvidovre Hospital]] — Surgical performance data recognizing the hospital for best practice in mortality reduction and high epidural usage.
- [[bispebjerg-og-frederiksberg-hospitaler|Bispebjerg og Frederiksberg Hospitaler]] — Acute surgery indicator results showing high unit compliance for epidural pain management.
- [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]] — Surgical metrics noting high compliance in postoperative observation and mobilization for high-risk patients.
- [[esbjerg-sygehus-grindsted-sygehus|Esbjerg Sygehus Grindsted Sygehus]] — Acute surgery data including specific 30-day and 90-day mortality statistics across reporting periods.
- [[esbjerg-sygehus|Esbjerg Sygehus]] — General mentions in regional quality improvement efforts for acute surgery in Region Syd.
- [[herlev-hospital|Herlev Hospital]] — Recognition as a best practice unit for exceptional longitudinal results in reducing acute surgery mortality.
- [[herlev-og-gentofte-hospital|Herlev og Gentofte Hospital]] — Detailed acute surgery indicator results, patient demographics, and mortality data.
- [[holbaek-sygehus|Holbæk Sygehus]] — Significant quality improvements serving as a reference unit for postoperative observation and early mobilization.
- [[hospitalerne-i-nordsjaelland|Hospitalerne i Nordsjælland]] — Acute surgery performance metrics and patient outcome data for the North Zealand hospital group.
- [[hospitalsenhed-midt|Hospitalsenhed Midt]] — Surgical outcomes identifying the Viborg unit as a best practice example for specific operational indicators.
- [[hvidovre-hospital|Hvidovre Hospital]] — Distinction as a best practice unit for sustained success in reducing 30-day postoperative mortality.
- [[kolding-sygehus|Kolding Sygehus]] — Data contributions to supplementary cancer disease analyses among acute surgical patients for risk adjustment.
- [[naestved-slagese-og-ringsted-sygehuse|"Næstved, Slagelse og Ringsted sygehuse"]] — Acute surgery metrics illustrating variance in epidural catheter usage and patient outcomes.
- [[nykoebing-f-sygehus|Nykøbing F Sygehus]] — Acute surgery indicators characterized by low patient volumes and high statistical uncertainty in mortality reporting.
- [[odense-universitetshospital-svendborg|Odense Universitetshospital - Svendborg]] — Surgical performance data and 30-day mortality statistics for the Svendborg unit.
- [[ouh-odense-universitetshospital-odense|OUH Odense Universitetshospital (Odense)]] — Extensive acute surgery patient data, demographic distributions, and outcome indicators for the main Odense unit.
- [[regionshospital-nordjylland|Regionshospital Nordjylland]] — Surgical metrics and audit feedback questioning indicator definitions and Charlson score applications.
- [[regionshospitalet-goedstrup|Regionshospitalet Gødstrup]] — Acute surgery performance including specific 30-day and 90-day mortality rates and process indicators.
- [[regionshospitalet-horsens|Regionshospitalet Horsens]] — Significant quality improvements, particularly achieving high rates of early postoperative mobilization.
- [[regionshospitalet-randers|Regionshospitalet Randers]] — Status as a best practice hospital with substantial quality improvements in acute surgery indicators over recent years.
- [[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] — Role as a tertiary center handling high-comorbidity acute surgery patients with distinct mortality profiles and audit findings.
- [[sjaellands-universitetshospital-koege|"Sjællands Universitetshospital, Køge"]] — Data contributions to national cancer distribution analyses used for risk-adjusting postoperative mortality.
- [[sjaellands-universitetshospital|Sjællands Universitetshospital]] — Broad acute surgery indicator results and patient outcome metrics for the Zealand University Hospital network.
- [[slagelse|Slagelse]] — Reporting on cancer disease distribution for risk-adjusting 90-day mortality indicators in the AKDB.
- [[sygehus-lillebaelt|Sygehus Lillebælt]] — Acute surgery performance data, including zero 30-day mortality for patients with a Charlson Score of 0.
- [[sygehus-soenderjylland|Sygehus Sønderjylland]] — Acute surgery metrics and noted regional quality improvements in postoperative mobilization.
- [[vejle-sygehus|Vejle Sygehus]] — Data contributions to supplementary analyses of cancer comorbidities in acute surgical patients.
